description: Interactive Resistance Bank Trainer Kit for practical study of series, parallel, and complex resistor networks, equivalent resistance (Rth) calculation, and Nodal Laplacian analysis.
aim: To construct various resistor networks (series, parallel, series-parallel, bridge) on the trainer board using jumper wires, calculate the theoretical equivalent resistance (Rth) between two measurement terminals by hand, and verify against the exact nodal Laplacian solver.
objective: Understand equivalent resistance calculation in series, parallel, and bridge topologies.
Practice jumpering circuit connections across physical through-hole resistors on a lab trainer.
Formulate node equations and apply Ohm's law / Kirchhoff's laws to complex resistor networks.
Learn to identify open circuits, short circuits, and redundant connection paths.
theory: In any resistor network, the total equivalent resistance (Rth) between two terminals A and B represents the single equivalent resistance that draws the same current from an applied voltage source. For resistors in series, current is identical and resistances sum directly: R_total = R1 + R2 + ... + Rn. For resistors in parallel, voltage across each branch is identical and conductances sum: 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/Rn. For general, non-reducible or bridge networks, nodal analysis using the conductance Laplacian matrix (G · V = I) solves for the exact terminal driving-point impedance.
working_principle: The Resistance Bank board consists of 15 precision through-hole resistors with gold-plated terminal sockets (numbered 1 through 30). By inserting jumper patch cords between sockets, students link resistor pins into electrical nodes. Connecting two resistor leads with a jumper places those two nodes at the same potential (shorted together). Any two sockets on the board can then be designated as measurement terminals Node A and Node B to calculate and verify the equivalent resistance.
apparatus: Resistance Bank Lab Trainer Kit (15 fixed through-hole resistors)
Set of flexible jumper patch cords / wire links
Digital Multimeter (DMM) for resistance measurement (Ohmmeter mode)
Calculators and notebook for manual nodal analysis
procedure: Select two or more resistors on the board to combine.
Insert jumper wires between socket terminals to link resistors in series, parallel, or a combination.
Designate two open sockets as measurement terminals Node A and Node B.
Calculate the equivalent resistance (Rth) between Node A and Node B by hand using series/parallel reduction or nodal analysis.
Enter Node A, Node B, and your hand-calculated Rth in the Practical Evaluation panel and check your answer.
precautions: Do not short circuit both terminals of a resistor with a single jumper unless intentionally bypassing it.
Ensure jumper pins are securely seated into socket jacks.
Make sure measurement terminals Node A and Node B are not shorted together (which results in 0 ohms).
Ensure there is a continuous electrical path between Node A and Node B through the resistor network.
